subsystems.name: Ultrasound transducer array
subsystems.role: generates and focuses ultrasonic waves through the skull onto a small patch of prefrontal cortex.
parts: piezoelectric elements (e.g., PZT ceramic or capacitive micromachined ultrasound transducers)

subsystems.name: Driving electronics
subsystems.role: produces the electrical signals that steer and shape the ultrasound beam.

subsystems.name: Head-worn frame
subsystems.role: holds the transducers against the scalp with stable acoustic coupling.
parts: adjustable mounts for individual head shapes

subsystems.name: Targeting and navigation
subsystems.role: aims the focus at the intended cortical target despite skull distortion.
parts: subject-specific head model from MRI or CT
optical or electromagnetic tracking (if real-time guidance is used)

subsystems.name: Safety and monitoring
subsystems.role: keeps ultrasound exposure within safe limits and detects unintended effects.

subsystems.name: Power and user interface
subsystems.role: supplies power and lets the user control sessions.

buildSteps.title: Model the acoustic path
buildSteps.detail: Using MRI or CT scans, simulate how ultrasound travels through the skull and where it focuses in the prefrontal cortex, adjusting for skull thickness and density.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the transducer array
buildSteps.detail: Dice a piezoelectric ceramic or micromachine a capacitive array, then bond matching and backing layers so the array produces a clean, steerable beam.

buildSteps.title: Build the driving electronics
buildSteps.detail: Design circuit boards that generate phase-shifted radio-frequency signals for each element, amplify them, and fit within a wearable power budget.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the headgear
buildSteps.detail: Integrate transducers, electronics, and cooling (if needed) into an adjustable headband that maintains acoustic contact without uncomfortable pressure.

buildSteps.title: Write control software
buildSteps.detail: Develop algorithms for beam steering, dose calculation, session timing, and safety cut-offs, plus a simple user interface.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and test in phantoms
buildSteps.detail: Measure the acoustic field in tissue-mimicking materials and verify that the focus matches the simulation.

buildSteps.title: Validate in animal and early human studies
buildSteps.detail: Run controlled experiments to confirm that stimulation changes prefrontal activity and to establish safe exposure levels.

buildSteps.title: Run sham-controlled clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Compare active versus inactive stimulation in tasks measuring attention and distractibility, looking for consistent, reproducible effects.

buildSteps.title: Scale manufacturing and seek regulatory clearance
buildSteps.detail: If trials succeed, set up production of transducers and electronics, and obtain approval as a medical or wellness device depending on claims.

prerequisites.why: Demonstrated in animals and small human studies to modulate cortical excitability, but effects on concentration are not yet established.
Current research systems are bulky; a wearable requires dense arrays and low-power electronics that are still being developed.
Precise focusing usually needs an MRI-derived head model; a consumer device would need simpler, low-cost alternatives.
Closed-loop stimulation could improve safety and effectiveness, but portable, reliable brain monitoring is still maturing.
Regulatory limits exist for diagnostic ultrasound, but neuromodulation doses and long-term effects need separate validation.

prerequisites.tech: Understanding of prefrontal cortex role in attention
prerequisites.why: The prefrontal cortex is known to support task persistence, but individual variability is large and stimulation effects are subtle.

pathway.milestone: Laboratory studies using transcranial focused ultrasound to modulate prefrontal activity
pathway.unlocks: Basic understanding of safe doses and short-term effects on brain circuits.

pathway.milestone: Sham-controlled trials in healthy volunteers and people with attention difficulties
pathway.unlocks: Evidence on whether stimulation reliably improves concentration.

pathway.milestone: Wearable research prototypes with integrated targeting and safety monitoring
pathway.unlocks: Practical experience with head-worn form factors and real-world use.

pathway.milestone: Regulated consumer or medical device, if benefits are proven and risks are acceptable
pathway.unlocks: Wider access to non-invasive cognitive stimulation, likely with safeguards and possibly clinical oversight.

pathway.milestone: Closed-loop systems combining stimulation with EEG or other feedback
pathway.unlocks: Personalized, adaptive stimulation that adjusts to the user's brain state in real time.
